MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 12, 2021
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on January 12, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on January 7, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Goodell joined
the meeting at 6:08 p.m.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were three cases to address for item CS1. The
Council did not get to the first one and there was no reportable action for the second matter. For the
third topic, Attorney Curley announced that the Council and community will be glad to hear that
despite there being a bit of risk, the City has come up with an affirmative and effective way to do
some blocking of the offensive language that has been displayed at political kiosks in the City. He
noted that he is looking at using the City's blinder rack law to block the language from youth and
he hopes that the community will find the solution to be positive.

For item CS2, staff provided the City Council with an update but there was no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

 P1. Presentation to Former Mayor Goodell

 P2. Opening Remarks by Mayor Kelley

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Rick Sandzimier, Saddleback Valley Men’s Golf Club (SVMGC) Board Member, M.V.: thanked
the City for hearing SVMGC’s interests, concerns and support for Oso Creek Golf Course and
offered to meet with the City to provide input during the vision plan process. He also requested that
SVMGC be provided a confirmed block of tee times on Saturday mornings.

Robert. D. Breton, M.V.: thanked the entire City Council for governing last year, during the
pandemic, with such resilience and tenacity. He said that Council Member Goodell was just the
right person to lead the City as Mayor in 2020 and he thanked him for his outstanding leadership
and for inspiring residents to carry on.

City Council Minutes  2  January 12, 2021

vaccine is available.

Bryan and Roxanne Spafford, M.V.: asked if the Mission Viejo City Council is working with the

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 16. Agreement with Retail Strategies for Business Attraction and Recruitment Consultant
  Services

  Council Member Sachs stated that he is opposed to this agreement due to the current
  coronavirus conditions. He said businesses are struggling to make it through and the idea
  of attracting new businesses to town at this time is remote, in his opinion. He also noted
  that he has asked for Retail Strategies’ working notes since the beginning of the current
  contract and they have not produced those notes. The firm has said that Mission Viejo is
  attractive to grocery stores and fast-food chains and he feels there are more opportunities
  that need to be identified. Council Member Sachs asked the Council to deny this request,
  bank the $50,000 and consider using the money for the Economic Development Committee
  to work on the Civic Core Vision Plan.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to deny
  the request and direct that the $50,000 be set aside for possible use by the Economic
  Development Committee for work related to the Civic Core project area.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell thanked his colleagues and Robert Breton for the nice comments about
his leadership as Mayor last year. He stated that it was a great time for him and a year of growth.
He also thanked the residents who brought up the topic of COVID-19 vaccines earlier in the
evening. The City does have a large senior community and he said it is important to stay on top of
vaccine opportunities. Council Member Goodell announced that at the next Council Meeting,
Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix will provide an update on the Inclusion
and Equity Committee which is combining the efforts of many existing organizations and adding
new things. He said he is anxious to see how the committee is coming together. Council Member
Goodell also announced that he was elected to the Orange County Transportation Authority
(OCTA) Board of Directors by the Orange County Mayors. He is very appreciative of the
appointment and said he will be overseeing bus, rail, freeway and major arterial connection
improvements for the County. He noted that he’s happy to serve alongside County Supervisor Lisa
Bartlett and Dana Point Council Member Joe Muller to help represent South County in making sure
that there are solutions that work really well for citizens in this area and all of the County. Council
Member Goodell provided a brief update on the 405 and I-5 freeway widening projects as well as
the extension of Los Patrones on the 241 as another southbound traffic mitigation alternative.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated Trish Kelley and Wendy Bucknum on their positions as
Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem and said it will be the year of women in leadership. He noted that Mayor
Kelley has an ambitious agenda for 2021 and he will do anything in his power to help so that the
Council can continue to make Mission Viejo a wonderful place to live.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs congratulated former Mayor Goodell on his service as Mayor last year and
stated that trying times call for leadership like Brian brought forward. He also congratulated former
Lieutenant Quyen Vuong on his well-deserved new title of Captain. He shared that the Council
Members have been receiving calls from residents over the past two months regarding vendor
booths in the City that sell political goods which are difficult to put up with when children are in
the car. Council Member Sachs noted that he got tired of explaining about State laws and the First
Amendment which allow for these political booths so he recently challenged the City Attorney to
find an answer. He thanked City Attorney Curley for doing a wonderful job in identifying an
opportunity that will help assuage some of the profanity and ugliness that goes on. Council Member
City Council Minutes  8  January 12, 2021
 Sachs further stated that while driving around the City he has noticed a lot of businesses are
struggling or are simply gone. He thanked his colleagues for approving the grant program to help
stressed businesses but said he wants to further challenge staff and the Council Members. He
proposed that every household in the City receive a $50 coupon to be used at Mission Viejo
restaurants and retail establishments, especially mom and pop businesses, and asked staff to come
back with ideas at the next Council Meeting.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum stated that she agrees with Council Member Sachs’ proposal and even
though a restaurant like McDonalds is part of a larger firm, most are owned by local franchisees
and they may be struggling too. She noted that she has updates for the next meeting on recent
activity at the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) and the Local Agency
Formation Commission (LAFCO). She also congratulated former Mayor Goodell on a job well
done last year. Due to the pandemic, he didn't have the opportunity to participate in a lot of the fun
ceremonial things that most Mayors do, however he had difficult meetings to attend and numerous
public service announcements and videos to create to keep the communication going. Mayor Pro
Tem Bucknum congratulated Mayor Kelley and said she loves the goals that she outlined for the
coming year. She also thanked all the healthcare providers who are so busy right now. Every facet
of medical professional is doing an amazing job and Council Member Bucknum expressed that the
City is with them and thanks them. She further thanked fire and police personnel who are dealing
with emergencies and are often exposed to coronavirus while doing their jobs. Mayor Pro Tem
Bucknum congratulated Captain Vuong on his promotion and Council Member Goodell on his
appointment to the OCTA Board which came after a unanimous nomination by the Orange County
Mayors. She said she is passionate about making sure that South County is not forgotten so she is
so pleased that Council Member Goodell has a seat at the table. In closing, Council Member
Bucknum urged residents to stay safe and healthy; keep bodies fueled, wash hands, wear a mask
and protect others. She also encouraged residents to practice unity, peace and kindness.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley thanked Karen Hamman for filling in tonight for City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt who
was unable to attend the meeting. The Council will recognize Karen at the next meeting before she
retires at the end of the month. Mayor Kelley said she has always thought of Karen as the “Dean of
City Clerks” because she is an expert and has truly been a valuable member of the City team and
City family. Mayor Kelley provided an update on the potential release of up to 1,800 prisoners from
the Orange County jail system after a lawsuit was filed by the American Civil Liberties Union
(ACLU). Mission Viejo joined several other Orange County cities in an Amicus Brief to support
Sheriff Barnes in his appeal. She said that nothing substantial has happened at this time but there
will be two more hearings at the end of the month and the City will keep a close eye on that. Mayor
Kelley also addressed concerns regarding the sidewalk vendors that were mentioned earlier. She
said State Senate Bill 946 expressly allows street vendors to occupy the public right of way and
prohibits cities from restricting them. The Council hopes to do more to limit how they display their
items for sale, especially those laced with profanity. Mayor Kelley announced that tomorrow there
will be a virtual grand opening ceremony for the Oso Parkway Bridge along the toll road. Residents
can tune in to watch on the TCA website, Facebook or YouTube channel. She also announced an
upcoming blood drive on January 19, 2021, from 12:00 to 6:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at
City Hall and she noted that all donors are tested for COVID antibodies. She reminded residents of
the City’s food drive on Saturday, January 16 from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. at the Murray Community
City Council Minutes  9  January 12, 2021
 Center and a food distribution event hosted by Saddleback Church on the first Saturday of each
month at Los Alisos Middle School. In conclusion, Mayor Kelley shared that the Community of
Character word for the month of January is perseverance.

Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of former Orange County Sheriff Shandra
Hutchens, to Tuesday, January 26, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.
